On-Chain Operator. Lesson 12.1, Your balance sheet. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already keep a journal and a kill rule. A balance sheet is that habit turned into accounts.
Assets: everything you own, at market value: collateral, yield positions, reserves.
Liabilities: everything you owe: loans, margin, any payables.
Liquidity runway = liquid reserve ÷ monthly obligations (spending + interest).
Banks fail from liquidity (can't pay today) more often than from solvency (owe more than they own).

Work the example on paper. $300,000 collateral, $60,000 debt at 5%, $40,000 stablecoin reserve, $5,000/month spending: defi_calc.py bank --collateral 300000 --debt 60000 --borrow-apy 5 --reserve 40000 --monthly-spend 5000 Equity $280,000 · LTV 20% · health factor 4.0 Obligations $5,250/month ($250 of it interest) → reserve covers 7.6 months Policy checks: LTV ≤ 30% ✓ · HF ≥ 2 ✓ · reserve ≥ 6 months ✓. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Balance sheet updated weekly. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Equity, LTV and runway tracked over time. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Policy limits written (max LTV, min HF, min runway). If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Assets $500k, debt $100k. Equity? The answer: $400k.
Check yourself. 2. Reserve $30k, obligations $6k/month. Runway? The answer: 5 months, below a 6-month policy.
Check yourself. 3. Why track liquidity separately from equity? The answer: You can be solvent and still be forced to sell at the worst time if you can't meet obligations today.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to build a personal on-chain balance sheet and read the three numbers that matter: equity, L.T.V.
First, Assets: everything you own, at market value: collateral, yield positions, reserves.
Next, Liabilities: everything you owe: loans, margin, any payables.
And finally, Liquidity runway equals liquid reserve divided by monthly obligations (spending + interest).
